Subject: Azure private plan onboarding - vendor security & procurement checklist

Maya / Laura,

Thanks for the call today. Procurement has a few outstanding items before they can route the Azure private plan through our finance team. Can you confirm the following items and return the completed questionnaire?

- SOC2 Type II report (most recent) or letter of attestation
- Completed vendor security questionnaire (attached)
- Point of contact for commercial / PO routing (Azure private plan flow differs from direct invoices)
- Confirmation of standard contract term (we typically need a sample purchase order and signature path)

Procurement would like the SOC2 evidence and a redlined copy of the private offer by end of week if possible so they can include it with the PO.

Attachment: Stellar_Security_Questionnaire_v3.pdf (please return as PDF)

Proposed next steps: if you can confirm who will sign (Redwood legal or sales) and provide the security materials, we will schedule a procurement review on Thursday.

Best,
Anna Park

Stellar Health

Anna -- thanks for the clear list. We're aligned and can move quickly.

Quick summary of what's attached:
- Redwood_Security_Questionnaire_Response.pdf: completed answers with references to our SOC2 evidence collection points
- redwood-azure-private-offer-draft.docx: our draft private plan commercial terms (no redlines yet)

A few notes up front:
- SOC2: we will provide our full Type II report under NDA. If procurement prefers an extract or bridge letter first, say the word and we can provide a scoped attestation.
- Billing flow: for Azure private plans the marketplace issues the invoice; customers typically route a PO to the seller and to Microsoft. We can provide the sample PO language (Net30 by default) and accept marketplace terms or a seller amendment if required.
- Signing: Redwood can accept DocuSign for the seller-side signature. If Stellar requires a separate master services agreement, please flag which exhibits need to be attached to the private offer.

Proposed next step: Ben (cc'd) will propose minimal commercial redlines for procurement to review. Karthik will prepare the attestation path for SOC2 delivery (link to secure share). Could we schedule the procurement review Thursday 6/17 at 11am PT?

Attachments: [Attachment: Redwood_Security_Questionnaire_Response.pdf], [Attachment: redwood-azure-private-offer-draft.docx]

Thanks,

Subject: Internal: Proposed redlines for Stellar Health private plan

Team,

I reviewed the draft offer and Stellar's questionnaire. Below are suggested redlines / talking points to keep the procurement convo moving while protecting our risk profile:

1) Data retention: propose explicit 90-day data purge after contract termination for customer-provided input and KV cache logs, with exception language for audit/legal holds.
2) Indemnity: suggest a mutual indemnity and cap at the greater of 12 months fees or $250k for tort/contract claims; push back on open-ended third-party IP warranties.
3) Acceptance & PO: recommend we accept Azure marketplace acceptance flow; require that Stellar send a purchase order referencing the private plan SKU within 30 days of DocuSign.
4) SLA: keep our standard 99.9% uptime target for Dedicated capacity; offer service credits but limit remedies to credits, not termination for single incidents.
5) SOC2 delivery: provide full report under NDA; offer a bridge letter for procurement immediate review while we finalize the secure share.

If that looks good I'll produce a tracked redline of the draft offer to share with Maya to send to Stellar. I also recommend attaching our seller onboarding checklist for Azure (helps them and shortens back-and-forth).

Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Commercial Ops, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
